## Setting and Framework

The present work is situated within the theory of o-minimal structures over the field of real numbers, a setting that provides a robust and flexible framework for tame geometry. Within this context, we consider a closed definable set $T$ together with a collection of projection maps whose fiberwise operations give rise to families of definable sets. More precisely, these projections allow one to associate to each parameter a corresponding fiber, and by varying the parameter one obtains structured families of definable sets. The interplay between the closed definable set $T$ and the projection maps is central to the constructions that follow, as it governs how the individual fibers are assembled into the collections whose topological invariants we seek to control.

## Main Results

The principal contributions of this paper are two quantitative bounds on the topological complexity of the fiber collections $\mathcal{A}_{\zeta}$, expressed in terms of the number of distinct topological types that can arise.

First, we prove the existence of a constant $C(T)$, depending only on the underlying set $T$, that bounds the number of distinct *stable homotopy types* of the collections $\mathcal{A}_{\zeta}$. Specifically, this number is bounded above by
$$
C \cdot n^{(k_1+1)k_2}.
$$
This result shows that, although the parameter may range over an infinite family, only a controlled, polynomially bounded number of stable homotopy types can occur.

Second, we establish an analogous bound for the number of distinct *homotopy types* of these same collections. In this case, the number of homotopy types is bounded above by
$$
C \cdot n^{(k_1+3)k_2}.
$$
The slightly larger exponent reflects the finer nature of the homotopy classification as compared with its stable counterpart, while preserving the same polynomial character of the bound.

## Relation to Prior Work

These theorems extend a line of results that had previously been established in more restricted geometric settings. In particular, bounds of the same type were known for semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian families. The present results generalize these earlier estimates to the broader and more general o-minimal setting, thereby demonstrating that the polynomial control on the number of topological types is not a special feature of these particular categories but rather a phenomenon intrinsic to tame geometry as captured by o-minimality.

We therefore present it in a form that we hope will be useful in other contexts as well.

# Bounding Homotopy Types in Definable Families over O-minimal Structures

## Introduction and Motivation

A fundamental problem in real algebraic geometry and its generalizations concerns understanding the topological complexity of families of sets defined by systems of equations and inequalities. When one considers a parametrized family of sets, a natural question arises: as the parameters vary, how many genuinely distinct topological configurations can appear? This question of bounding the number of distinct homotopy types has deep connections to computational complexity, quantitative topology, and the theory of definable sets.

This paper investigates precisely this question in the general framework of o-minimal structures. O-minimal structures provide an axiomatic setting that captures and unifies many well-behaved classes of sets, including semi-algebraic sets, semi-Pfaffian sets, and subanalytic sets, among others. By working at this level of generality, our results simultaneously encompass and extend a variety of previously established bounds that were proven separately for these more specific settings.

## Main Results

The central contributions of this paper are polynomial upper bounds on two related but distinct invariants associated with definable families. Given a definable family parametrized in a manner that depends on integer complexity parameters $k_1$ and $k_2$, together with a scaling parameter $n$, we establish the following:

**Stable homotopy types.** We prove that the number of distinct stable homotopy types occurring in the family is bounded above by
$$
C \cdot n^{(k_1+1)k_2},
$$
where $C$ is a constant depending only on the ambient data of the family and not on $n$.

**Homotopy types.** For the finer classification by ordinary homotopy type, we establish the bound
$$
C \cdot n^{(k_1+3)k_2},
$$
where again $C$ is an appropriate constant independent of $n$.

The difference in the exponents—$(k_1+1)k_2$ versus $(k_1+3)k_2$—reflects the fact that homotopy type is a strictly finer invariant than stable homotopy type, and consequently more configurations can be distinguished, requiring a correspondingly larger bound.

## The Key Technical Tool: A Topological Comparison Theorem

The technical heart of our approach is a topological comparison theorem, which serves as the essential bridge enabling the passage from geometric data to homotopy-theoretic conclusions. The comparison theorem allows us to relate the homotopy type of a given definable set to that of a suitably constructed model or approximation whose complexity can be directly controlled by the defining parameters.

The strategy proceeds by showing that, up to the relevant notion of equivalence (stable homotopy equivalence or homotopy equivalence), each member of the family can be replaced by a representative drawn from a controlled finite collection. By counting the number of such representatives—which depends polynomially on $n$ with exponents governed by $k_1$ and $k_2$—we obtain the desired bounds on the number of distinct types. The comparison theorem ensures that this replacement does not lose the topological information we seek to enumerate, so that bounding the number of models yields a genuine bound on the number of homotopy types.

## Relation to Previous Work

Our results generalize and unify several bounds that appear in the existing literature. In the semi-algebraic setting, bounds on the number of homotopy types of families defined by polynomial inequalities have been studied extensively, providing quantitative refinements of classical finiteness theorems. Similarly, in the semi-Pfaffian context—where sets are defined using Pfaffian functions, a class encompassing many transcendental functions with controlled complexity—analogous bounds have been established.

By recasting these questions within the o-minimal framework, we demonstrate that the underlying phenomena are not specific to the algebraic or Pfaffian structure but instead flow from the general tameness properties guaranteed by o-minimality. This perspective not only recovers the earlier semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian results as special cases but also extends them to any o-minimal structure, thereby covering a substantially broader range of definable families under a single unified argument.

## Conclusion

In summary, this paper establishes polynomial bounds on the number of stable homotopy types and homotopy types occurring in definable families over arbitrary o-minimal structures. The bounds $C \cdot n^{(k_1+1)k_2}$ and $C \cdot n^{(k_1+3)k_2}$ capture the way in which topological complexity grows with the defining parameters, and the topological comparison theorem provides the crucial mechanism translating geometric control into homotopy-theoretic enumeration. By situating these results in the o-minimal setting, we provide a general and conceptually clean framework that subsumes prior semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian results and clarifies the essential role of tameness in governing the topology of parametrized definable families.

# Abstract

We establish uniform bounds on the number of homotopy types occurring among the fibers of a definable family in an arbitrary o-minimal structure. Given a definable family $\{A_t\}_{t \in T}$ of definable sets, where $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \times T$ and $A_t = \{x : (x,t) \in A\}$, we prove that the fibers $A_t$ realize only finitely many homotopy types as $t$ ranges over the parameter space $T$. Moreover, we show that the number of distinct homotopy types is bounded by a constant depending only on the combinatorial complexity of the defining formula, and not on the particular o-minimal structure in which the family is interpreted.

Our approach combines the cell decomposition theorem with a definable triangulation argument, yielding effective bounds in the semialgebraic and subanalytic settings. When the family is defined by polynomial (in)equalities of bounded degree, we recover and refine the classical estimates of Milnor–Thom type, obtaining a bound polynomial in the number of defining conditions. As applications, we derive uniform finiteness results for the Betti numbers of definable fibers and for the number of connected components, and we discuss consequences for the theory of parametrized definable families, including quantitative results on definable trivializations. The uniformity across o-minimal structures follows from a transfer principle for the underlying combinatorial data, and we illustrate how these bounds specialize in structures such as $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{an}}$ and $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$.

---

counterfactuals.output:
Here is a formal abstract written in LaTeX, suitable for a research article in o-minimal geometry.

```latex
\documentclass[11pt]{amsart}

\usepackage{amsmath, amssymb, amsthm}
\usepackage{mathtools}

\begin{document}

\begin{abstract}
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be an o-minimal structure over a real closed field $R$, and
fix a closed definable set $T \subseteq R^{\,\ell} \times R^{k} \times R^{n}$.
For each $\mathbf{y} \in R^{\,\ell}$ we consider the fibre
$T_{\mathbf{y}} \subseteq R^{k} \times R^{n}$ and the induced family of
projections onto $R^{n}$, giving rise to the definable arrangement
$\mathcal{A}(T_{\mathbf{y}})$ whose members are the images
$\pi\!\left(T_{\mathbf{y}} \cap \left(\{\mathbf{x}\} \times R^{n}\right)\right)$,
$\mathbf{x} \in R^{k}$, together with the Boolean cells they determine in
$R^{n}$. Our principal result asserts that, as $\mathbf{y}$ ranges over the
parameter space $R^{\,\ell}$, the number of distinct homotopy types realised by
the arrangements $\mathcal{A}(T_{\mathbf{y}})$ is bounded by a polynomial in
$n$, with degree and coefficients depending only on $T$ (equivalently, on
$\ell$, $k$, and the ambient complexity of the defining formula) and not on
$n$. More precisely, writing $h_{T}(n)$ for the number of homotopy types so
obtained, we prove
\[
    h_{T}(n) \;\leq\; C(T)\, n^{\,d(T)},
\]
where $C(T) > 0$ and $d(T) \in \mathbb{N}$ are effectively bounded in terms of
the data defining $T$.

The argument proceeds by combining a uniform triangulation of definable
families with a fibrewise analysis of the semialgebraic (respectively,
definable) monotone families of sets that arise under projection, refining the
classical stratification techniques of Hardt-type trivialisation into a
quantitative statement compatible with the tameness axioms of $\mathcal{S}$.
A key ingredient is a bound on the number of connected components and on the
higher Betti numbers of the sets in $\mathcal{A}(T_{\mathbf{y}})$ that is
polynomial in $n$ and uniform in the parameter $\mathbf{y}$; this is derived
from a spectral sequence associated to the nerve of the projected family,
whose terms are controlled by the o-minimal Vapnik--Chervonenkis machinery.
The polynomial dependence on $n$ is shown to be sharp in the sense that, for
suitable $T$, matching lower bounds hold, so that the exponent $d(T)$ cannot in
general be reduced.

Our results extend the polynomial bounds previously known in the
semialgebraic and semi-Pfaffian categories to the full generality of arbitrary
o-minimal structures, and eliminate the exponential dependence on $n$ present
in bounds obtained by naive cell decomposition. As applications we deduce
polynomial bounds on the number of homotopy types of fibres of definable maps,
on the combinatorial complexity of definable hypergraph arrangements, and on
the number of distinct isotopy types of configurations arising in
o-minimal families, thereby providing effective tameness estimates relevant to
computational real geometry and to the model-theoretic study of definable
families.
\end{abstract}

\end{document}
```

**Notes on the construction.** The abstract is framed around the canonical objects of o-minimal geometry—definable sets, projections, and homotopy types—and states a clean polynomial bound $h_T(n) \le C(T)\,n^{d(T)}$ with uniformity in the parameter $\mathbf{y}$. It sketches the proof strategy (uniform triangulation, Hardt trivialisation, a nerve spectral sequence, VC-type bounds), asserts sharpness, and situates the result relative to the semialgebraic and semi-Pfaffian literature. You can adjust the notation ($\ell, k, n$) or specialize the structure $\mathcal{S}$ (e.g., to $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$ or $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{an}}$) to match the exact scope of your article.

# Bounding Homotopy Types of Definable Arrangements

## Abstract

We prove effective upper bounds on the number of distinct stable and ordinary homotopy types realized by arrangements of hypersurfaces defined by a fixed number of polynomials of bounded degree, and more generally by definable sets in an o-minimal structure. Given a family of such arrangements parametrized by a definable set, we show that the number of homotopy types occurring in the family is bounded by an explicit function of the combinatorial data—the number of defining equations, their degrees, and the ambient dimension—independent of the coefficients themselves. Our results extend classical bounds on the number of connected components and Betti numbers to the finer invariant of homotopy type, and separate the behavior of the stable homotopy type from that of the ordinary homotopy type. The central technical ingredient is a **topological comparison theorem**, which guarantees that after a suitable definable triangulation, the homotopy type of an arrangement is determined by the sign conditions realized by the defining polynomials, allowing us to reduce a continuous question to a discrete enumeration.

## 1. Introduction

The study of quantitative and effective bounds in real algebraic geometry has a long and fruitful history, originating with the work of Oleĭnik–Petrovskiĭ, Milnor, and Thom, who bounded the Betti numbers of a real algebraic set in terms of the number and degrees of its defining polynomials. More recently, attention has turned from bounding the *invariants* of a single set to bounding the number of distinct *isomorphism types* that can arise across an entire family of sets sharing the same combinatorial description. Results of this kind—counting connected components, isotopy types, or homeomorphism types up to the discrete data of degrees and dimension—provide a robust measure of the geometric complexity intrinsic to a class of definable objects.

In this paper we address the finest homotopical version of this question. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote an arrangement of hypersurfaces, or more generally a definable set built from a bounded number of polynomials of bounded degree in an o-minimal expansion of the reals. As the coefficients vary, the arrangement deforms continuously, and its homotopy type may change; yet intuitively only finitely many such types can occur. We make this precise and quantitative for two distinct notions of equivalence:

- **Ordinary homotopy type**, the equivalence induced by continuous homotopy equivalences between the underlying spaces; and
- **Stable homotopy type**, the coarser equivalence obtained after passing to suspension spectra, which discards unstable phenomena and is often more accessible to systematic control.

Our main theorem asserts that both counts are bounded by an explicit function of the number of defining equations, their degrees, and the ambient dimension, uniformly in the coefficients. The distinction between the two bounds is genuine and instructive: the stable homotopy type admits sharper and more transparent estimates, reflecting the additive, spectrum-level structure that governs it, while the ordinary bound must account for the additional rigidity of unstable homotopy theory.

The key technical tool underlying both results is a **topological comparison theorem**. Roughly speaking, this theorem shows that the homotopy type of a definable arrangement is a function only of the *sign conditions*—the discrete pattern of vanishing and inequalities—realized by its defining polynomials, provided one works up to a controlled definable triangulation. By establishing that homotopically equivalent sign conditions yield homotopy equivalent (respectively, stably equivalent) arrangements, the comparison theorem converts the problem of enumerating homotopy types into the combinatorial problem of enumerating realizable sign conditions, for which effective bounds are available through the theory of Thom–Milnor type estimates and their o-minimal generalizations.

The remainder of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2 we fix notation and recall the necessary background from o-minimal geometry and homotopy theory. Section 3 is devoted to the statement and proof of the topological comparison theorem. In Section 4 we derive the bounds on stable homotopy types, and in Section 5 we treat the ordinary case, highlighting where the two arguments diverge. We conclude in Section 6 with applications and open questions.

---

*Note: This draft assumes a real algebraic / o-minimal setting; if your paper concerns complex arrangements, hyperplane arrangements specifically, or a different technical framework, let me know and I can retune the terminology, the form of the comparison theorem, and the cited antecedents accordingly.*
